seo.meta_title: What Happened to Beef-A-Roo? 2026 Closures Explained
seo.meta_description: Beef-A-Roo closed its Rockford-area restaurants and others in 2026 amid payroll problems. What happened, who owns it now and which locations may reopen.

question: What Happened to Beef-A-Roo?
quick_answer: Beef-A-Roo had a rough 2026. After payroll problems and unpaid fundraising checks, the Rockford, Illinois, chain closed all eight of its company-owned Rockford-area restaurants, temporarily closed seven more in other states, laid off staff in July and took its website offline. Since then, new operators have stepped in: local business owners Bob Grottke and Alex Edwards are working to reopen Rockford locations, and a company called BAR II Op-Co says it has secured Beef-A-Roo sites in five states. A few independently owned locations, like Freeport, Illinois, stayed open.
key_facts: Grew to nearly 30 locations after a 2019 sale
New operators are working to reopen locations

body.heading: A Rockford original
body.text: Dave DeBruler and Jean Vitale opened the first Beef-A-Roo in Rockford, Illinois, in 1967, serving roast beef and ham sandwiches. The chain became known for its themed restaurants, such as log cabins, fire stations and diners, and for roast beef and cheddar fries. After Dallas private equity firm Elysian Capital bought it in 2019, Beef-A-Roo expanded to nearly 30 locations in several states, including Missouri, Indiana, Kansas, Arkansas and Michigan.

body.heading: What went wrong in 2026
body.text: Trouble started early in the year with reports of unpaid fundraising contributions to Rockford-area schools and groups. In spring, Rockford stores briefly closed after the company fell out of compliance with the Illinois Department of Revenue, and the company blamed accounting issues. By June, employees said they hadn't been paid for weeks, and some locations closed. In July, Beef-A-Roo laid off staff, and its website went offline on July 8.

body.heading: Which locations closed
body.text: All eight company-owned Rockford-area restaurants closed, and seven more locations in Missouri, Indiana, Kansas and Arkansas were closed at least temporarily during what the company called a restructuring. Elysian Capital told employees it planned to sell the chain to a Texas firm. Not every Beef-A-Roo shut down: the Freeport, Illinois, location is independently owned and stayed open.

body.heading: Is Beef-A-Roo coming back?
body.text: There are signs of a comeback. Bob Grottke, owner of Tom & Jerry's, and Alex Edwards of Candy Cloud teamed up to buy and reopen Rockford-area locations, starting with the Alpine Road store. Separately, BAR II Op-Co says it has secured Beef-A-Roo locations in Illinois, Missouri, Indiana, Arkansas and Kentucky, with more under negotiation, and plans to let experienced managers own and run individual stores. Reopening dates vary, so call ahead.

body.heading: What Beef-A-Roo serves
body.text: Beef-A-Roo's menu is built around roast beef sandwiches, burgers, chicken sandwiches, loaded potatoes, cheddar fries and shakes. Our Beef-A-Roo menu page shows the last known prices, but check with your local restaurant, since menus and prices may change under new owners.

faqs.a: Many locations closed in 2026, including all company-owned Rockford-area stores. Some independently owned locations stayed open, and new owners are working to reopen others.
Payroll problems, unpaid fundraising checks and tax compliance issues led to closures and layoffs in 2026.
Elysian Capital bought it in 2019 and planned to sell it in 2026. New operators, including BAR II Op-Co and Rockford owners Bob Grottke and Alex Edwards, are reopening locations.
